summary: The single finding is confirmed, with a narrower fix. The accepted map's QSeriesPartitionsAndMockModularForms examined note ('moonshine applications do not state a code-stage input') is now stale. The QSeries packet gap for the FLM moonshine module (added 2026-09-24 in #2875, a day after this map's review) names AlgebraicCodingTheory Layers 5–6 as the Golay/Construction-A input to a Leech lattice that no atlas roadmap constructs. The map was right when it was reviewed. The mathematical guard is right: 2e_i lies in P_2(C) for every binary code and has B_2-norm 2, so P_2(G24) has roots and is not the Leech lattice. Narrowing: no overlap entry and no link. The QM.6 atlas stage text does not name coding, the only evidence is a partial, unreviewed packet gap, and the direction is not in doubt. The fix is a rewritten examined note plus one requests entry. Hypothetical L5/L6 → QM.6 edges would be acyclic (checked), but none is authorized. FF.4 is not touched.

findings.reason: Confirmed, with a narrower fix. Evidence checked. (a) The map's examined entry for QSeriesPartitionsAndMockModularForms reads verbatim: 'Theta/partition and moonshine applications do not state a code-stage input; the coding roadmap excludes theta-series development.' (b) The QSeries packet (status partial, SHA-256 177eaefe…050bc, equal to the red team's hash) has a gap titled 'The Frenkel–Lepowsky–Meurman moonshine module V♮ and its Monster action'. Its neededBy lists QM.6/monster-head-characters and QM.6/monstrous-moonshine-theorem, and its detail says the construction needs 'the Leech lattice (no roadmap of the atlas constructs it; AlgebraicCodingTheory Layers 5–6 supply the Golay code and Construction A)'. The same sentence is at readmes/QSeriesPartitionsAndMockModularForms.md line 3823. (c) The finding is right to call this staleness, not an author error. git -S dates the sentence to #2875 (2026-09-24), while the map was accepted on 2026-09-23. The QM.6 atlas stage text still names no coding input (its requires are ModularCurvesPartII:R12.3, QM.1 and UPSTREAM:RepresentationTheory). (d) The Leech gap is real. IntegralLattices (README L20–21) excludes Niemeier/Leech constructions, and coding excludes rank-24 glue tables and classification. No atlas roadmap, packet or link map constructs it: 'Leech' occurs only in the QSeries packet, this map, and exclusion lines in IntegralLattices, StablePeriodicCurved and ZigzagPreprojective. No QSeries link map exists that could carry the handoff. (e) The guard is right. Under the standing convention B_m(x,y)=(Σx_i y_i)/m on P_m(C)=ρ_m⁻¹(C) (README L80–85), 2e_i reduces to 0 ∈ C, so 2e_i ∈ P_2(C) with B_2(2e_i,2e_i)=4/2=2. P_2(G24) is the even unimodular rank-24 lattice with 48 roots ±2e_i, not the rootless Leech lattice. The standard Leech construction from G24 needs a further step: the sublattice with coordinate sum ≡ 0 mod 4, then a glue vector. Construction A alone does not give it. The existing ACT-R05 already says this. The finding's Shimada citation was not needed for this and was not re-read. (f) Cycle test: adding either coding Layer 5 or Layer 6 → QSeriesPartitionsAndMockModularForms:QM.6 to the 3,458 atlas stage-edges plus every link map's links (4,163 distinct edges) creates no cycle. That edge is still not authorized, because QM.6 consumes the Leech lattice, not Construction A, and the intermediate owner is missing. Corrections to the fix. (1) Do not add an overlap. §10 uses overlaps when the texts leave the direction unsettled, and here the direction (coding supplies, moonshine consumes, through an unowned Leech step) is not in doubt. Also, the only evidence is an unreviewed packet gap, not two stage texts. The GN.4 precedent (ACT-O03) differs: GN.4's own stage text names FF.4. (2) Authorized scope: (i) in examined[QSeriesPartitionsAndMockModularForms], keep result 'none'. Replace the note with: the QM.6 stage text states no code input; the partial, unreviewed QSeries packet gap for the FLM moonshine module names coding Layers 5–6 (Golay code, Construction A) as inputs to an unowned Leech lattice; no link is recorded; see the new request. (ii) Add one requests entry, e.g. ACT-R06, owner QSeriesPartitionsAndMockModularForms, stages coding Layer 5, coding Layer 6 and QM.6, status unresolved_consumer_contract. It says: the Leech lattice (rank 24, even, unimodular, rootless) has no owner in the atlas and needs one, to be decided by the maintainer under PROTOCOL §15, without expanding IntegralLattices or coding in place. Its construction from G24 imports the coding Golay code and Construction A but is not P_2(G24) (cross-reference ACT-R05). A directed edge into QM.6 (or into the Leech owner) is added only once that owner and the rational-to-real comparison contract are fixed and the QSeries packet is reviewed. (iii) Optionally, one clause in the top-level summary. No links, overlaps, coding or IntegralLattices README text, or QSeries packet content change. Severity: medium is at its upper edge. Nothing coding builds changes, but an unowned prerequisite of a planned theorem is a real routing gap. Disclosure: this verifier wrote FIX-RT-AREA-finitefields (PR #4632), which touched FF.4 coding ownership. This finding and verdict do not touch FF.4, L08–L09 or O03.
